findings.problem: Every `x ∉ (synCen).fv` fact is proved by naming `fv_syn_cen` explicitly and then closing with a hand-written `nb076_compact_fv_empty_*` lemma. Those helper lemmas are just `x ∉ (∅ : Finset Var)`, which core `Finset.notMem_empty` already provides as a simp lemma. The `Explicit` variant `fv_syn_cen` used here has no `@[simp]`, although its twin in `CompactSyntaxFV` does. So plain `simp` cannot reduce `g ∉ (synCen).fv` to `True`. This forces the `simpa only [...] using ...` pattern in each of the 14 theorems, plus a separate `nb076_compact_fv_empty_*` family.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `fv_syn_cen` and the other closed-term `fv_syn_*` lemmas in `CompactSyntaxFVExplicit.lean` with `@[simp]`, matching `CompactSyntaxFV.lean` (or register them in the already-opened `CoreFVSimp`). Then each `nb076_wpp_notmem_*` follows from `by simp`. Better, state one generic lemma `x ∉ (synCen).fv` (`fun x => by simp [fv_syn_cen]`) and drop the per-variable `nb076_compact_fv_empty_*` and `nb076_wpp_notmem_*` copies in favour of `fun _ => ...` arguments to `TEnvFresh.consFresh`.
findings.benefit: Callers get a canonical normal form, `(synCen).fv = ∅`, with automatic membership discharge. This removes about 14 near-identical lemmas and the dependence on the numbered `nb076_compact_fv_empty_*` helpers, and it keeps the two parallel `fv_syn_*` APIs consistent.
